Threat.value: Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience
Being superalert or watchful or on guard

Memory.value: When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop
I can't seem to put the frightening event into words.
Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory

issues.item: Threat: Risky Behavior: Taking too many risks or doing things that could cause you harm
issues.explanation: For a police-related trauma, the combination of threat items is not fully coherent: startle response and physical reactivity fit PTSD, but risky behavior is a different symptom style and is weakly connected to the rest of this profile. With only Threat and Memory represented, risky behavior lacks support from the other selected items and does not read as a clear trauma-linked threat perception.

issues.item: Memory: Guilt on Recall: When I remember the event I feel intense guilt
issues.explanation: Within Memory, the items suggest overwhelmed, poorly verbalized traumatic recall, which is coherent for PTSD. However, intense guilt on recall introduces a strong negative appraisal theme that is otherwise absent from the profile. Given the formulation only shows a Threat → Memory link and no active Negative Appraisals connections, this item is not well aligned with the stated cognitive pattern.

vignette: Kofi's eyes still scan the room with an intensity that makes his wife, Ama, worry. It's been two years since the incident with the police, but the way he flinches at every sudden noise, the way his shoulders tense when a stranger approaches him on the street - it's as if his body has learned to expect danger around every corner. As a curriculum designer, Kofi spends most of his days in front of a computer screen, but even the familiar hum of the office can't calm the hypervigilance that has become second nature to him. When memories of that night resurface - and they do, often without warning - Kofi feels like he's drowning. He'll be working on a project, lost in thought, when suddenly the sound of sirens or the smell of asphalt will transport him back to the scene: his hands cuffed behind his back, the officer's knee pressing into his spine, the feeling of helplessness that threatened to consume him. It's not just the image that overwhelms him - it's the emotions that come flooding back, unbidden and intense. Kofi has tried to put the experience into words for Ama, but every time he attempts to recount what happened, he finds himself stuck on a single, searing detail: the look in the officer's eyes. Sometimes, the memories come without any clear image at all - just a wave of anxiety that crashes over him, leaving Kofi breathless and disoriented. It's as if his body remembers the trauma even when his mind can't quite grasp it. When this happens, Ama tries to be patient, but she can see the fear in her husband's eyes, the way he struggles to ground himself in the present moment. She knows that Kofi is trying to make sense of what happened, to find a way to process the emotions and memories that still haunt him. As time has passed, Kofi has become more adept at avoiding triggers - no news programs or cop dramas for him - but it's hard to avoid the world entirely. And when he does venture out, his hypervigilance is always on high alert, scanning for potential threats. It's exhausting, and Ama worries that one day he'll just shut down completely. The other night, Kofi had a nightmare so intense that he woke up drenched in sweat, his heart racing like it used to when the police first approached him. That's what finally brought him to seek help - the realization that two years on, the memories still have the power to consume him whole. Kofi is afraid of losing himself completely, of becoming a shadow of the man he once was. He hopes that therapy will give him back some sense of control over his life, over his memories and emotions. For now, though, the past remains a raw, open wound - one that still has the power to startle him awake in the dead of night.
